newsitem.title: USA: House panel approves $115 billion in Medicare cuts.
newsitem.headline: House panel approves $115 billion in Medicare cuts.

text.p: A key House of Representatives panel easily approved a bipartisan plan Monday to save $115 billion from Medicare over five years.
The vote was 36 to 3, with three Democrats dissenting.The Medicare savings are a key component in a plan agreed by the White House and Congress last month to balance the federal budget in five years.

The plan would avert the imminent bankruptcy of Medicare's hospital fund trust and keep it solvent for a decade until the year 2007. But the reforms to the programme do not address the difficult problem of how Medicare will cope with the crush of baby boomers retiring early in the next century.

Most of the savings in the five-year plan come from limiting payments to doctors, hospitals and other health care providers. The plan also offers Medicare patients more options such as health maintenance plans and tax-free medical savings accounts.
Medicare covers 38 million Americans, including everyone 65 and over, and some disabled persons.
